title: How Long Are Thanksgiving Leftovers Safe? A Simple Guide
seoTitle: How Long Are Thanksgiving Leftovers Safe to Eat?
excerpt: Thanksgiving leftovers are safe for three to four days in the fridge, or two days by UK guidance. Here are the storage rules, reheating temperatures and signs to throw food out.
content:
Quick answer: Cooked Thanksgiving leftovers keep for three to four days in a refrigerator kept at 40 degrees F (4 degrees C) or below, following the US Department of Agriculture. UK guidance from the Food Standards Agency is stricter, and says eat leftovers within 48 hours. After the time limit, or if a dish has sat out for more than two hours, throw it out. Reheat to a steaming 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

Thanksgiving 2026 leaves a lot of food in the fridge, and most of it is safe for days, not hours. The trick is knowing which dishes last, how to store them, and when a leftover becomes a risk. This guide uses current food-safety guidance from the US and UK so you can decide with confidence rather than guesswork.

How long do Thanksgiving leftovers last in the fridge?

For cooked poultry, stuffing, gravy and casseroles, the safe window is short. The US Department of Agriculture's rule of thumb is three to four days for cooked leftovers held at 40 degrees F or colder. That means a roast carved on Thanksgiving Thursday is best finished by Sunday, and at the outside by Monday.

The UK is more cautious. The Food Standards Agency advises eating leftovers within two days and freezing anything you will not manage in that time. If you are serving guests who are pregnant, older, very young, or have a weakened immune system, follow the two-day guidance; those groups are more likely to become seriously ill from food poisoning.

LeftoverUS guidance (fridge)UK guidance (fridge)
Turkey and other cooked poultry3 to 4 days2 days
Stuffing and casseroles3 to 4 days2 days
Gravy1 to 2 days2 days
Cooked vegetables and sides3 to 4 days2 days

Gravy is the odd one out. Because it is a liquid with no structure to slow bacterial growth, food-safety bodies treat it as the most perishable leftover and suggest using it within one to two days.

How quickly must leftovers get into the fridge?

The two-hour rule is the one that catches people out. Both the FDA and the Food Standards Agency say perishable food should not sit at room temperature for more than two hours, and the limit drops to one hour when the room is above 90 degrees F (32 degrees C). For Thanksgiving that matters: a turkey left out while people graze through the afternoon can pass the two-hour mark without anyone noticing.

The fix is to get food into the fridge promptly, but not while it is still hot. The Food Standards Agency advises cooling cooked food at room temperature and placing it in the fridge within one to two hours. Speed the cooling by dividing large dishes into shallow containers, so the middle cools as fast as the edges.

How should you store leftovers?

Three habits cover most of the risk. First, refrigerate within the two-hour window and keep the fridge at or below 40 degrees F. Second, store food in covered containers or sealed bags, and place raw or drippy items on the bottom shelf so juices cannot contaminate other food. Third, label what you put away with the date, so you are not guessing on Sunday whether the turkey was cooked on Thursday or Friday.

Do not crowd the fridge. Cold air needs to circulate, and an overpacked refrigerator cools unevenly, which is exactly the condition bacteria need. The FDA warns that spills, especially drips from thawing meat, should be wiped up straight away to stop cross-contamination.

Can you freeze Thanksgiving leftovers?

Yes, and freezing is the better choice when you know you will not finish a dish in time. Freeze leftovers as soon as possible rather than waiting until the end of their fridge life, cool them first, and divide them into portions before freezing so they freeze quickly and thaw evenly. Turkey freezes well for two to three months; gravy and stuffing also freeze, though their texture softens slightly.

A freezer set at 0 degrees F (-18 degrees C) pauses bacterial growth rather than killing bacteria, so frozen leftovers are not safe forever for taste, even if the safety risk is low. Eat frozen Thanksgiving food within a couple of months for the best quality.

How do you reheat leftovers safely?

The target is simple: reheat to 165 degrees F (74 degrees C), steaming hot all the way through. That is the temperature at which the USDA says poultry and cooked dishes are safe, and it is the same figure to aim for whether you use an oven, a microwave or a pan. Stir food midway through microwave reheating so there are no cold spots where bacteria survive.

Reheat only what you plan to eat. Every time a dish is warmed and cooled again, it spends more time in the temperature range where bacteria multiply fastest. If you are unsure whether a portion was fully reheated, do not cool it and try again later; eat it now or throw it out.

What if guests want to take food home?

Send leftovers home cold, not warm, and give guests the same rules. Pack food into a covered container as soon as the meal ends, keep it chilled until they leave, and tell them to put it in the fridge within two hours of arriving home. A dish that spends a long car journey at room temperature is the classic way people get sick the day after Thanksgiving.

The FDA applies the two-hour rule to takeaway food and doggy bags exactly as it does to home leftovers. If the trip home will run long, a cool bag or an ice pack is a small effort that keeps the food in the safe zone.

When should you throw leftovers out?

Throw food out if it has passed its time limit, if it sat out for more than two hours, or if it looks or smells off. The FDA's advice is blunt: when in doubt, throw it out. Mold, slime, a sour smell or a change in colour are all reasons to bin a dish rather than risk it.

One mould myth is worth clearing up. You cannot rescue a tub of leftovers by scraping the mould off the top, because the mould's roots can reach deeper than the visible growth. For soft or liquid leftovers, that means the whole dish should go.

Frequently asked questions

How long is turkey safe in the fridge after Thanksgiving?

Three to four days on US guidance, or two days on UK guidance, as long as the fridge stays at 40 degrees F (4 degrees C) or below and the turkey was refrigerated within two hours of cooking.

Can you eat Thanksgiving leftovers if they were left out overnight?

No. Food left out overnight has spent many hours above the safe temperature, and the two-hour rule means it should be thrown away, not reheated.

Is it safe to reheat leftovers more than once?

Best practice is to reheat only once. Reheating a dish, cooling it and reheating it again gives bacteria repeated chances to grow, so reheat single portions and eat them.

How long does gravy last in the fridge?

Gravy is the most perishable Thanksgiving leftover. Aim to use it within one to two days, and freeze it if you want to keep it longer.

What temperature should leftovers be reheated to?

165 degrees F (74 degrees C), steaming hot all the way through, measured or checked in the thickest part of the dish.

This article covers food safety guidance from public health authorities. It is general information, not medical advice.
